symptom: alter snippet/page answered 'widget not found' for every widget inside a list view's specialization template (`template for M.Spec { … }`), in check and exec, though the alter-page skill documents them as ordinary named widgets; `accordion1 item@1` inside the template was refused as 'navigation list not found'.
cause: findInWidgetChildren walks every container shape (Widgets, FooterWidgets, scroll regions, layout grid, TabPages, Cells, nav Items, control bar, pluggable object lists) except a list view's Templates[]; the scope and nearest-data-source walkers had the same gap. The item-address miss message assumed every owner is a navigation list.
fix: Descend into Templates[] in the widget finder, the widget scope and the data-source walk; in the last, a template hands its Entity down as the context, so widgets inserted there bind to the specialization rather than the list view's generalized source. The item-address miss now says 'widget %q not found'.
insight: The page mutator has three parallel walkers (find, scope, nearest data source) that each enumerate container shapes by hand; a new shape must be added to all three. Grep for one existing shape ("TabPages") to find them. Templates also change the entity context, which a plain descent would have got wrong silently.
test: mdl/backend/pagemutator/listview_template_widgets_2173_test.go TestListViewTemplateWidgetsAreAddressable (control: a widget in the default body, scoped to the list view's entity)
